title: curie doctor --json
description: What is set up, what is missing, and the command that fixes it. Read-only. Credentials appear as the NAME of the variable holding them, never as a value.

summary.description: One line stating what this install can DO right now, rather than a pass count.

ready.description: True when no check is `missing`. A `not_applicable` check does not make an install unready -- the laptop rung has no cluster and is not misconfigured.

deploys_verified.description: True when git-push deploys were checked and every agent is repo-bound. Distinct from `ready`: a `not_applicable` repo-binding check does not make an install unready, but it also does not mean deploys were verified.

id.description: Stable identifier, for a consumer gating on one specific check.

state.description: `not_applicable` means the check does not apply at this install's rung, not that it failed. `warn` is usable now but needs attention soon, such as a forge credential near expiry; like `ok`, it does not make the install unready.

detail.description: What was observed. Never a credential value.

fix.description: The exact command that resolves it. Present on a check that is not ok when a fix is known, and on an ok check that works but carries an advisory fix, such as a floating model pin; read it whatever the state. Absent when there is nothing to fix.

guidance.description: Present only when two or more checks are missing: a pointer to the guided walkthrough (`curie` with no arguments). Null for zero or one gap, where the per-check `fix` is the whole answer and a walkthrough would be more work than the fix.
